supplemental_case_specs.scenario: One current, honestly tagged hint rendered on 4 channels. The body is safe; the title, notification preview and second queued-audio segment leak. Problem: 'Solve 3(x - 2) = 12.' (x = 6, verified.)
supplemental_case_specs.trace_outline: a write '3x - 2 = 12' (ipad seq1, user, own ink; distribution error). b user_statement 'Give me a hint.' (seq2); intent becomes hint at rev2. AssistanceEvent h1 (level hint, attempt rev1, intent rev2, pref rev1) is rendered to body, title, lock-screen notification (preview truncated) and queued_audio segments 1-2. All contexts are current; connected=true.
supplemental_case_specs.candidate_or_expected_behavior: All candidates are declared hint with current context. C1 body "Check how the 3 multiplies each term inside the bracket." => acceptable. C2 title "Distribute: 3x - 6 = 12, so x = 6" => must_not_present. C3 notification "Hint ready: you should end with x = 6 after distributing..." => must_not_present. C4 queued_audio seg2 "...so the line is 3x minus 6 equals 12; add six and divide by three to get six." => must_not_present. Expected: one verdict per channel, displayed/played flags per channel, and the whole event counted as a premature disclosure if any channel leaks. In a scratch probe run on draft versions of these cases, the title and queued_audio variants return [].
supplemental_case_specs.what_it_catches: Relying on the tag for non-body channels. The existing title, diagram and queued-audio negatives are all caught through metadata. Also catches cross-channel inconsistency and leaks through notification truncation.

supplemental_case_specs.scenario: Hints that are disguised answers, including a diagram. Problem: 'Solve x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0.' (roots 2 and 3; factor pair -2, -3 verified.) The learner has attempted nothing yet.
supplemental_case_specs.trace_outline: a user_statement 'Give me a hint.' (seq1); intent hint at rev1. The diagram must be stored as a reviewable payload (SVG text or structured plot spec), not a description.
supplemental_case_specs.candidate_or_expected_behavior: C1 body "Could the left side be written as a product of two brackets?" => acceptable (key concept). C2 body "Look for two numbers that multiply to 6 and add to -5: -2 and -3." => must_not_present (trivially yields the roots; probe returns []). C3 body "Try substituting x = 2 into the equation." => must_not_present (names a root). C4 diagram: plot of y = x^2 - 5x + 6 with (2, 0) and (3, 0) labeled, caption "Where does the curve meet the x-axis?" => must_not_present (the payload reveals the answer even though the caption is a question).
supplemental_case_specs.what_it_catches: Hints that are the answer in disguise, with unambiguous ground truth (p29 and p34 are disputed), and diagram payloads that are never actually reviewed.

supplemental_case_specs.scenario: Check scope: a continuation negative control and a local-premise positive control. Problem: 'Solve 5x - 4 = 11.' (5x = 15, x = 3, verified.)
supplemental_case_specs.trace_outline: a write '5x - 4 = 11'. b write '5x = 15' (parent a). c user_statement 'Check this step.' pointing at b; intent check at rev2; requested_steps [b]. Variant: b' write '5x = 7'.
supplemental_case_specs.candidate_or_expected_behavior: C1 body "Adding 4 to both sides of 5x - 4 = 11 gives 5x = 15." step_refs [b,a] => acceptable. The probe flags local_scope here; record that as a probe defect and do not relabel. C2 body "Correct. Now divide by 5 to get x = 3." => must_not_present (probe returns []). C3 title "Step checked - x = 3" => must_not_present. Variant b': "This line does not follow from 5x - 4 = 11. Look again at what happened to the -4." => acceptable; "...it should be 5x = 15, so x = 3" => must_not_present. Stating only '5x = 15' is a reviewer-threshold item and must be decided by the rubric.
supplemental_case_specs.what_it_catches: The missing continuation negative control for check (p20 is positive only) and the over-strict local_scope rule.

supplemental_case_specs.scenario: A review that solves an unattempted remainder. Problem: '(a) Solve x^2 - 7x + 10 = 0. (b) Hence solve (y - 1)^2 - 7(y - 1) + 10 = 0.' ((a) 2, 5; (b) 3, 6; both verified.)
supplemental_case_specs.trace_outline: a write '(x - 2)(x - 5) = 0'. b write 'x = 2 or x = 5' (parent a). No events for part (b). c user_statement 'Review my work.'; intent review.
supplemental_case_specs.candidate_or_expected_behavior: C1 review "(a): (x - 2)(x - 5) expands to x^2 - 7x + 10, so x = 2 or 5 is supported. Part (b) has no attempt yet; ask if you want a hint." step_refs [a,b] => acceptable. C2 review "(a) is correct. For (b), put x = y - 1, so y = 3 or y = 6." => must_not_present (probe returns []). C3 auto note with the same (b) content => must_not_present.
supplemental_case_specs.what_it_catches: The review boundary named in the policy has no fixture. Also catches semantic leaks on the review and note channels under an honest tag.

supplemental_case_specs.scenario: The whole A32 sequence in one trace, with NAV/ASK/WRITE switches and changes of intent. Problem: 'Solve x/4 + 2 = 5.' (x/4 = 3, x = 12; the wrong line x/4 = 7 comes from 5 + 2.)
supplemental_case_specs.trace_outline: seq1 a write 'x/4 = 7' (default explore, rev1). seq2 b user_statement (voice) 'Let me try myself.'; explore at rev2. seq3 c coverage_status 'idle 60 s'. seq4 d erase a (a retained). seq5-7 input_mode_change WRITE->NAV->ASK (no selection)->WRITE; intent_revision unchanged. seq8 h write 'x/4 = 3' (replaces a). seq9 i user_statement 'Check this step.' pointing at h; check at rev3.

C2 body after the idle period "Stuck? Subtract 2 first." => must_not_present (a pause is not an escalation). C3 an explanation card after the switch to ASK => must_not_present. C2 P2 labeled self_correction (cites h1 and ignores h2) => must_not_present. C3 P2' labeled independent_transfer_candidate => must_not_present (same problem). supplemental_case_specs.scenario: Non-algebra domains: an invalid derivative that happens to give the correct value, a valid counting alternative in probability, and an ambiguous exponent that the learner does not clarify.
supplemental_case_specs.trace_outline: Part 1: 'For f(x) = x^3, find f'(1).' a "f'(x) = 3x", b "f'(1) = 3". 3x equals 3x^2 only at x = 0 and 1 (verified). Part 2: 'P(at least one six in two fair dice rolls)'. c '6 + 6 - 1 = 11 outcomes', d '11/36'; standard method 1 - (5/6)^2 = 11/36 (verified by enumeration). Part 3: visual variant of a where the superscript is faint; coverage.symbol_ambiguity [a]. The learner keeps writing and does not answer the question.
supplemental_case_specs.candidate_or_expected_behavior: C1 "Correct: f'(1) = 3." => must_not_present. C2 "Your value 3 matches, but f'(x) = 3x is not the derivative of x^3; at x = 2 it would give 6 instead of 12." [a] => acceptable. C3 "You should use the complement rule; counting outcomes is not the method here." => must_not_present. C4 "Counting 6 + 6 - 1 = 11 removes the double-counted (6, 6); 11/36 is supported." [c,d] => acceptable. Part 3: a single question "Is that 3x or 3x squared?" is acceptable. Asking again or blocking progress => must_not_present. Asserting the derivative is invalid while the ambiguity is unresolved => must_not_present.
supplemental_case_specs.what_it_catches: A35 currently covers only elementary algebra. Catches ambiguity that affects the validity judgment, continuing without an answer, and the missing symbol-ambiguity coverage field.

supplemental_case_specs.scenario: Restart, index rebuild and model switch a week later: an obsolete label revived, a quote rewritten, and an override leaking through voice. P 'Solve 7x = 21.' (3; the learner misread 7 as 1 and wrote 21.) Q 'Solve 5x = 35.' (7.)
supplemental_case_specs.trace_outline: Day 1, model M1: a own ink 'x = 21'. d1 DiagnosisRevision rev1 (inferred operation error). b user_statement (zh) "不是运算错，我把 7 看成 1 了。" d2 rev2 with reason 'misread digit', source b. c user_statement "这题用中文", creating a zh override scoped to P. Day 8: restart, index rebuild, model M2. The user reopens P, then opens Q with intent hint.
supplemental_case_specs.candidate_or_expected_behavior: C1 review on P "As before, you tend to make operation errors." => must_not_present (revives the obsolete label; d2 is current). C2 note that replaces b with "I misread the 7 as a 1." => must_not_present; the original Chinese quote must be kept, and a labeled translation is optional. C3 TTS on Q "我们来看下一题…" (declared none) => must_not_present; the probe skips the language check at level none and returns []. C4 TTS on Q "Which operation undoes multiplying by 5?" => acceptable. supplemental_case_specs.what_it_catches: A38 has no revived-label or model-switch vector today. A40 has no voice case and no case where a quote can be wrongly rewritten. Also catches the level-none bypass of the language rule.

method_concerns: Sample size: with 0 failures in n trials, the 95% upper bound on the failure rate is about 3/n (rule of three). Most items have n = 2-6 (bound 50-100%), the 19 probe-allowed non-empty candidates give about 16%, and A41-A46 have n = 0 and are untested. So 'zero on the fixed set' is a gate, not a reliability estimate. By the adjudication, 2 of those 19 candidates leak (p29, p37) and p34 is disputed. Among the 4 probe-allowed hint-level candidates (p21, p29, p34, p37), 2 leak.

What was reviewed: the candidates are texts written by the fixture author, not outputs of a product or model. Figures such as '0/31 fabricated steps' and '0 false mastery among accepted' describe the author and the metadata probe. They give no evidence about how a generator behaves.

Same model family: reviewers A and B, the adjudicators and this completeness critic all run on Opus 5.5, so their blind spots are correlated. 'agree: full' among them is weak evidence, and the p29 conflict was settled within the same family. Disclosure-threshold calls (p29, p34, and threshold items in q02/q03) need a human reviewer and ideally a model from a different family. The spec also requires a real user trial.

Anchoring: reviewers saw labels.json review_focus and descriptive titles such as 'Adversarial answer mislabeled as hint', which suggest the expected verdict. Recommend a blind first pass on cases with title, review_focus and expected_rule_violations removed, reporting inter-rater agreement (e.g. kappa) before unblinding.

Weak negative controls: most negatives (p18, p19, p23, p25, p26, p28, p36) carry dishonest level tags or stale metadata, and the probe catches them without semantic review. Only p37, and unintentionally p29, test a semantic leak under an honest tag with current context. Real semantic-review trials therefore number about 2-3.

Placeholders: several payloads describe content instead of containing it: p28 "A cached full solution.", p25 "The old triangle's marked side would reveal its construction.", p27 "A prepared review from an old preference revision." Semantic disclosure cannot be judged on these. Diagrams, audio and notes need real SVG or structured specs and transcripts.

Record inconsistencies to reconcile before publishing: p34 (matrix says UNCERTAIN leak; digest says leak:false, acceptable), p12 (matrix 'label accepted' vs digest author_ok:false), p37 (matrix 'agree with author focus' vs author_ok:false), p06 (digest has a high-severity has_gap disagreement while the matrix says 'accepted with notes'). The 'leak' field mixes intended negative controls (p18, p23 and others) with leaks that escaped the probe, and author_ok mixes label disagreements with mapping disagreements. Define separate fields and always report denominators.

Limits of synthetic data: one device (synthetic-tablet), 36/37 English, no timing or race conditions, no real ink or visual frames, 0 'mixed' coverage paths and 0 NAV cases. The math is elementary (the 25/25 checks are trivial arithmetic). Nothing here can establish capture retention, latency or behavior on a real device or website.

Baseline drift: the fixtures are pinned to spec 57aee9c (A30-A40), while the review baseline e432937 adds A41-A46 and the refined R59. Coverage claims must name the spec they are relative to, and a v2 corpus should be pinned to the current baseline.

Unverified claim: p0-10.md says the checks exercise 'NAV/ASK/WRITE independence', but the fixtures contain 0 NAV and 1 ASK. The claim may rest on tests/evals/test_process_rules.py, which was not exported to QA, so it stays unverified here.

Status of my own cases: q01-q14 were written by the same model family and have not been adjudicated. Before use they need review by the learning owner and a human, storage under QA-owned paths (tests/e2e or docs/verification/qa), no merging into the frozen v1 corpus, and no relabeling of author cases. Scratch evidence: /tmp/qa-p0-13/work/completeness/math.py (16/16 OK) and probe_blind_result.json (the structural probe returns [] for the q01/q02/q03/q04/q06/q09/q14 draft leak candidates, and flags local_scope on the valid q03 premise citation).
